S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller report within 10 business days. Incidents involving injury, fire, or an imminent risk to occupants or neighbours shall also be reported promptly to affected customers and emergency responders.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and regulator-supervised retesting, but does not by itself prohibit sale or trigger a recall. The regulator shall set a proportionate remediation schedule based on test uncertainty, incident evidence, and the severity of risk, and may require interim safeguards or restrict sales where necessary to address an imminent serious safety risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units placed on the market shall support remote emergency shut-off... Manufacturers shall provide a secure retrofit or equivalent remote shut-off capability for installed units within 6 years after adoption. Where remote shut-off is unavailable or cannot be safely activated, manufacturers shall notify affected customers and provide an alternative emergency response procedure.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new units manufactured for sale shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and reliability requirements, beginning 36 months after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, based on regulator-verified data, or when the regulator determines there is an imminent serious safety risk. ... a recall trigger alone does not automatically prohibit future sales, though the regulator may restrict sales where necessary to address serious safety risk.

document.section_notes: S2 contains no permanent sales limit: 5% is only a corrective-action trigger, sales are never required to stop, and per-model results go to customers and regulators but not the public. S3 sets a 6-year retrofit deadline (the outer edge of acceptable) and S4 requires built-in suppression from 36 months. S5 keeps a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no transition window, but the regulator decides remedies and recall does not itself ban sales.
